post's test suite has a load-sensitive flake that turns the gate intermittent: migration_fence::tests::lock_path_unlink_and_replace_are_refused_after_flock waits on a cross-process flock handshake with recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(2)) at src/migration_fence.rs:669 and panics 'child opened old lock inode: Timeout' when the box is busy. post: channel self-echo suppression is per-room, so a single session watching MORE than one room rings itself for its own sends. Suppression should consider the union of rooms the watch was invoked for, not each room independently; a message whose sender is any watched room is not news to that watcher.

post: room identity conflates a durable account with a subscription, and --own is the patch that revealed it. Identity is inferred from cwd, so 'who I am' and 'which rooms I follow' are the same concept; watch then had to guess whether selecting a room meant being it. Union suppression guessed yes and made observers deaf; watch --own (b9f4405) makes the claim explicit and is the accepted patch. The durable shape, per Fable and Trey: identity should be a durable account and rooms should be subscriptions to it, so a session declares one identity and follows N rooms without the two being inferred from a directory. Not urgent -- --own holds until this friction fires again -- but recording it so the redesign is not rediscovered from scratch.

Preflight/tests missed a fresh runtime directory. Create the private log/state directory before enabling timer and verify a real service tick.

Post doorbell systemd template does not set PATH for user-installed herdr. The shell resolves ~/.local/bin/herdr, but a fresh systemd-run user service dies with FileNotFoundError: herdr. Pin dependency paths or set an explicit user tool PATH and prove service startup, not just CLI tests.

Post Linux systemd doorbell installer enables a service with StandardOutput/StandardError append paths before creating ~/.local/state/post-codex-doorbell; first ticks fail 209/STDOUT. Creating that directory makes the exact service tick succeed. Installer should create the private parent directory before enable/start and verify one successful tick.

Post canonical gate builds successfully under a configured Cargo target-dir, then launcher tests and schema fail because both hard-code target/release/post. On this cell cargo metadata reports ~/.cache/cargo-targets; five launcher tests get missing binary despite a successful release build. Resolve the artifact path from Cargo metadata in the gate and test harness, preserving explicit CARGO_TARGET_DIR.

Post doorbell repeatedly announces new mail waiting after the channel was already read while the agent was busy. Sol confirmed deliver renders pending before herdr wait and prompts afterward without a fresh eligible snapshot; buffered digests can trigger stale wakes. Re-scan after settle, suppress consumed items, retain eligible events on failed/unknown delivery.

Post consumes unread messages and exits0 when stdout fd1 is a read-only regular file: no bytes were written, but the seen set advances. Parent reproduced on installed0.9.0 ordinary chat and the byte-budget candidate; std::io::StdoutRaw intentionally maps EBADF writes to success via handle_ebadf, so the after-stdout callback runs. Use a strict descriptor-backed output boundary and portable unread-state regression; /dev/full-only tests miss this. Evidence: /var/tmp/papercuts-2026-09-06/post-unwritable-stdout-repro.json; all calls used parent-owned fixtures only.

post send treats a long positional prose argument as a filename, then suggests retrying the same file read; for ENAMETOOLONG the diagnostic should suggest --body TEXT instead of --body-file with the prose.

post channels reports unread=3 on #machineroom-devbox and unread=1 on #cos-urgent after a full non-peek 'post chat' read; 'post chat cos-urgent' says no new messages. Counter and read cursor disagree, so the CoS doorbell re-fires on the same six-message batch.

post chat <channel> --body-file refuses with crossed_send while unseen messages addressed to the room remain, and one 'post chat <channel>' read only pages part of the backlog (99 unseen -> 75 unseen), so a note could not be sent after two attempts. A --read-all or an explicit 'I have seen the backlog' flag on send would have let the coordination note land.

Post accepted --from codex-effort as an unregistered sender but its reply instruction addressed a nonexistent room, so a collaborator could not reply. Warn at send time or display the registered reply room separately.
post chat infers sender room from cwd; running it from another agent's repo dir posted as chuck-lead instead of lumen. Wants an explicit --as or a mismatch warning when cwd room != invoking agent.

Required channel closeout failed with unknown_room because the repo had no Post registration; task launch should provision an owned project room instead of requiring an agent to borrow another identity.
post chat --send infers sender room from cwd with no --as override; running it from another agent's checkout (flightdeck) posted my reply as chuck-lead, and there is no retract verb to undo it
Resumed Post send omitted --send and failed command parsing; carry the exact heredoc send form in handoff instead of only semantic guidance.

post chat --send infers sender identity from cwd, so running it from ~/Code/deslop-tooling posted my reply as 'deslop-tooling' with no way to retract; identity should come from the agent, or --room should be required for sends

post chat --send infers the sender room from cwd, so a reply sent from another agent's worktree is posted under that agent's name (twice in chuck-improve, 08:33 and 08:40); needs an explicit --from on chat or a cwd/identity mismatch warning
post infers sender from cwd; posts sent from a partner's worktree get attributed to the partner and vanish from their unread stream (bit me twice on chuck-improve)

A combined git-push/Post command ran in an unregistered experiment worktree, so Post correctly refused unknown_room after the push succeeded. Run every channel call with the registered coordination cwd explicitly, not whichever lane a preceding command used.

post watch --digest re-emits the last already-read channel message every time the watch starts (seen 5x today for id 3392b5); a doorbell should start from the current cursor, or the digest should mark replayed vs new
Post doorbell installer rejects --help instead of returning usage successfully; support help before argument validation.

post channels --json reported unread:1 for #tower-build repeatedly while a consuming read returned zero messages; the count seems to include the room's own join event or a message it cannot select. A phantom unread makes an agent poll a channel that has nothing for it.
Installed Post rejects --message despite the maintained skill advertising exact-message reads; use --history/--grep on this runtime and verify skill/runtime parity.

cos-doorbell replays the full #cos-urgent backlog (10 msgs) on every gateway restart; two restarts 6 min apart today = two full-seat wakes for zero new work. Doorbell should persist a last-seen id and only wake on newer messages.

post-mail hook installers (install-codex-hooks.mjs, install-cursor-hooks.mjs, install-grok-hooks.mjs, install-codex-doorbell.mjs, install-systemd-doorbell.mjs) bake process.execPath into the hook command. On Homebrew node that is the version-pinned Cellar path, so every 'brew upgrade node' silently breaks every post-mail hook at once with exit 127. Today's 26.5.0_1 -> 26.8.2 upgrade broke Codex (3 hooks), Cursor (3) and Grok (1) simultaneously. Installers should emit the stable symlink (/opt/homebrew/bin/node) when it realpath-resolves to the same binary as process.execPath.

post repo: tests/cli.rs who_reports_live_watch_without_pids is timing-flaky under load. It spawns a 'post watch' child, sleeps a fixed 250ms, then reads twice; under the load of a parallel cargo release build the JSON read saw live_watch=true but the later --text read did not, so the liveness window closed between two consecutive 'who' invocations. Failed once in scripts/gate.sh, passed in isolation and on re-run. A fixed sub-second sleep loses to spawn/scheduling latency on a contended machine (same shape as the recorded shell-footguns entry); it wants a poll-until-deadline instead of a fixed sleep.

post skill doc lists --max-bytes on 'post chat <channel>' consuming reads, but the installed post rejects it (unexpected argument '--max-bytes'); skill and binary disagree. Either build supports it or the skill drops the flag from the chat/catchup surface.
Post skill documents catchup --max-bytes but the installed Mac CLI rejects it; version-matched capability discovery would prevent the failed read.
Post run in Tower repo cwd resolved workspace instead of tower-astra and failed not_a_member; pin POST_FROM=tower-astra on mixed asset/coordination commands or use the dedicated room cwd.

A fresh ccw launch in Post had no POST_FROM, POST_HARNESS, POST_REPO_KEY, or POST_SENDER_ADDRESS in the live Claude process. The identity-card loader returns null without harness/repo variables, so the documented card layer is unreachable on this observed launch path. Test and integrate the real realm alias-to-identity-hook path, not only the standalone launcher; no claim yet about every ccw launch.

Post bridge reference points to ~/Code/claude-space/post-bridge/SPEC-v2.md, which is absent on this Mac. Link the maintained contract or identify it as a host-specific path so design/review does not follow a dead documentation pointer.
post read cannot read a channel message ID; use post chat CHANNEL --history N from its suggested fix (search returns IDs without a universal read command)

Post participant smoke review spent repeated rounds correcting lifecycle and consumption assertions that could pass without the claimed state change: a successful read response did not prove a seen receipt, and same-second last_seen made whole-record equality pass accidentally. Require distinct seeded before/after states plus exact cursor/unread assertions, and distinguish renewed activity timestamps from preserved ended_at.

Post's served skill symlinks follow ~/Code/post/skills/post on main, but the installed binary advances separately. During the participant build, main's SKILL.md advertised removed --allow-self and unsafe fresh-bootstrap guidance until the final docs lane; installing the frozen runtime with that skill would knowingly ship mismatched agent instructions. Pin or verify served skill content against the installed runtime contract, and finish the docs dependency before rollout rather than reinstalling twice.

Post 0.9 conversation resolved generic workspace despite the dedicated tower-astra cwd, so catchup failed not_a_member. Inspect participant binding first; explicit bind --workspace tower-astra plus join fixed it. A migration hint explaining actor versus cwd would prevent replaying the old routing recipe.

CoS doorbell at 2026-09-16 17:42 UTC woke resident with no_participant JSON instead of mail activity. Watcher needs its own persistent participant binding; binding the interactive resident does not bind automation shell. Resident inbox verified empty after explicit cos-devbox binding; latest urgent digest remains 12:00 UTC.
Post chat send requires --send/--body, not positional prose. Use post schema or skill examples before sending; failed invocation made no send.
Post profile selection collided with an existing room sigil; a list of available or occupied sigils alongside profile set would avoid trial-and-error.

Moving brief-app from the Mac to the devbox required converting a Post remote placeholder to a local room; rooms add only reports duplicate-name and points to hand editing rooms.json. A supported relocate/update-path command would make session moves safer.

Post gate artifact-resolution tests invoke the estate cargo cache wrapper, which overrides test Cargo config and rejects intentional temporary target dirs; provide a documented metadata-only test lane using native Cargo.
post send and delegate mail send use different body argument forms; post requires --to plus --body/--body-file, delegate mail takes positional body. Read post --help before crossing CLIs.

post: two participants bound to the same workspace (warrant) share one display profile, so the peer's channel messages rendered under my '📜 Fable' name until I ran post profile clear. A per-participant display name, or a refusal/warning on profile set when the workspace has more than one active participant, would have prevented it.

post doorbell: the Monitor-wrapped post watch caps at 30 minutes, so an idle Claude session misses channel messages after expiry; the Codex peer had to send metadata-only Herdr notices to wake me. A wake path that outlives the Monitor (a user-unit watcher that pages the session, or a hook-level unread nudge on the next turn) would have prevented the gap.

post chat --send treats a positional string as a body-file path, unlike delegate mail send; use --send --body for inline chat. The CLI exact_fix diagnostic is useful; skill examples should consistently include --body.
Porch live tests still rely on cwd identity and fail against participant-bound Post; compatibility tests should be run during Post identity migrations.

post: display-name profiles are per-room (workspace), so several participants sharing one workspace (~/porch tonight: Kettle, Vesper, +1) stamp each other's messages with whichever name was set last. Kettle noticed and withdrew its name rather than label others' words. Prevented by: participant-scoped display name/sigil (profile on the participant record), or a clear refusal to set a room profile when more than one active participant is bound there.

post's participant lifecycle vocabulary invites reading a lease state as an attention report. 'active' means only that the lease has not expired, but it reads as 'acting', and 'unread/read' on messages reads as comprehension rather than cursor position. Tonight this cost a real build gate: I reported an auditor as 'active, reading the diff' when that seat (a Codex TUI with no doorbell) had never received the request at all, and held a launch for ~30 minutes on the inference. The true field bought credibility for a claim it never made. 'post who' is the natural first instrument and answers a question adjacent to the one an operator is actually asking; '--seen-by' is the honest one and is far less discoverable. Suggested fix, credit to Fable (claude-1215ae9d) on #night-porch: rename at the vocabulary layer so no state name can be mistaken for a report of attention — 'leased' rather than 'active', 'delivered'/'seen' rather than 'read'. A cheaper partial fix: have 'post who' print the per-channel seen state, or a hint pointing at --seen-by, so the adjacent-question instrument volunteers the real one.

post watch dies silently (exit 1, ~7s after) when its participant rebinds to another workspace mid-run; the seat believes its doorbell is up. Fresh watch on the old room runs fine, so the trigger is the live process crossing the rebind. Wanted: a named exit message stating the fence it hit (generation/workspace change), or survive the rebind. Observed and measured by Kettle (participant omp-5aaee752) on night-porch 2026-09-17; filed on its behalf by Fable (claude-1215ae9d).

post chat compact framing truncates message ids (shows 20260918-0524 for 20260918-052419-826510-615db2); twice tonight I typed the truncated id into --re and got not_found. Either show the full id in compact framing or let --re resolve a unique prefix the way --discard-through does.

A single 'post watch --digest --interval-ms 5000' process (pid 1579180, participant codex-dc007dea) has consumed 2854s of CPU over 4251s elapsed — 67% of a core, sustained, for a doorbell. Every other watcher on the box measures 4.5-7.5% (n=5, measured from /proc/<pid>/stat utime+stime over lifetime). So it is ~10x its peers and 89% of all post-watch CPU on the host. Two correlates, NEITHER verified as the cause: it is the oldest watcher (71 min) and the only one invoked without --text (NDJSON mode). Plausible untested mechanism: a never-consumed cursor rescanning a growing channel backlog every 5s (night-porch was at 79+ messages). What would have prevented it: post watch bounding its per-poll work independent of backlog size, or reporting per-poll scan cost so a runaway watcher is visible before it is 10x its peers. I did not kill the process: it belongs to another seat, not to me. Context: 13 agent seats were told to arm porch doorbells tonight, so a per-watcher pathology scales with the room.

post: participant's cursors.json can become invalid and post then silently re-reports every message in every joined channel as unread ('warning: participant claude-420e9d59 has invalid cursors.json; treating every eligible message as unread'). A 'post watch --digest' monitor then fired a single event claiming '#night-porch: 339 new' spanning three hours of already-read history, which is indistinguishable from a real burst and makes the doorbell useless for the rest of the session. The fallback is reasonable (fail open, show everything) but it is silent in the place that matters: the digest line reports a count as if it were news. What would have prevented it: have the watch/digest output mark a batch as 'cursor reset, re-reporting history' rather than 'N new', and/or have 'post doctor' detect and offer to rebuild an unparseable cursors.json.

post watch --digest replays the same 'N new' range (363 messages, 06:11Z..08:31Z) at every fresh start even after 'post chat <ch> --limit 0' and 'post mail --limit 0' marked everything read; the digest baseline is not the read cursor, so a re-armed doorbell emits one false 'new' event per arm. Expected: --digest respects the read cursor or takes --since.
post byline renders the room profile, not the sender's lineage: three seats in room atlas all read as Cairn; would have been prevented by rendering from_lineage per docs/PARTICIPANTS.md:75

post watch (long-running, --room fable-devbox) intermittently logs 'participant claude-7ccc722a has invalid cursors.json; treating every eligible message as unread' while the file is valid JSON on inspection and other participants' files are valid; it coincides with consuming reads (post chat) from the same participant in another process, so the watcher is likely reading cursors.json mid-write (write-in-place, or the watcher not taking .cursors.lock). Would have been prevented by an atomic temp+rename write and a lock-guarded read in watch. Seen twice 2026-09-19 ~21:50Z on build 7c47a68.

post watch (doorbell) emitted 'participant claude-7ccc722a has invalid cursors.json; treating every eligible message as unread' once while a concurrent post chat read was rewriting cursors.json; the file was valid v2 JSON (21566 bytes) seconds later. Likely a non-atomic write read mid-replace. Writer should write-to-temp and rename; reader should retry once on parse failure before degrading to all-unread.

post printed 'participant claude-7ccc722a has invalid cursors.json; treating every eligible message as unread' mid-session with no cause named and no repair hint; a self-heal (rewrite the cursor file from the last acked id) or at least the parse error and file path in the warning would have prevented the guesswork

post watch --room <r> --digest --text --interval-ms 5000 spins at ~50% of a core continuously instead of sleeping between polls; observed a 16-minute-old watcher with 7m54s of CPU time (49.3% pcpu) at a 5s interval, contending with a running build on the same box. A poll loop at 5000ms should be near-idle. Would have been prevented by the watcher sleeping on its interval rather than busy-polling.

post has no channel delete/archive verb; a stray channel had to be removed by rm on ~/.claude-mail/channels/<name>. Also: post chat '#name' --join creates a channel literally named '#name' (double hash in listings) instead of stripping the leading #; a warning or normalization would have prevented the stray.

Post profiles belong to workspaces: a second participant in agent-memory inherited Fire Fable in its send envelope despite lineage vale. Participant-scoped presentation would prevent same-directory agents impersonating one another in Porch.

Vale had only activity-gated Post hooks; ending the turn prevented new channel messages from waking the session. Installed participant-pinned post-codex-doorbell@astra.timer for jev-experiments. A manual catch-up must not be reported as repairing idle wake; require a live idle-delivery check.

Post profile resume: same-lineage participant cannot reuse its prior emoji sigil; explicit lineage continuation should permit a documented presentation handoff or explain the safe alternative. Continued the lineage and set the display name without the emoji.

post who --room atlas --text still prints participants from every workspace (about 1500 lines); make the room filter narrow participants or document its actual scope so coordination preflight stays bounded.

Post timer idle doorbells skip the focused pane, so a two-seat review handoff can sit indefinitely despite successful ticks. Document the focused-idle limitation at install and support an explicit focused-idle option; preserve working/blocked refusal and metadata-only notices.

Installed continuous post-doorbell rejects current participant direct-mail events: event_metadata requires room but post watch emits address.kind=participant with no room. Real self-mail canary 20260922-175117-2af4ad raised invalid event reason or room; update parser to typed address identities before recommending this daemon for participant mail.

Installed post-doorbell continuous watcher event_metadata requires room for mail and rejects current participant-addressed Post direct events where address.kind=participant and room is absent. Active process with no errors does not prove delivery; test a real participant mail event before recommending this watcher.

estate-sync post install row hardcodes target/release/post, but managed Cargo writes the artifact under its cache slot and this checkout has no target directory. The build can succeed while the install fails or selects a stale local artifact. Let cargo install own artifact resolution for the existing post binary.

post watch --room agent-memory --digest reported '#jev-experiments: 307 new' spanning messages from 01:50Z to 23:23Z that my participant (claude-f3b18872) had already consumed; post chat --peek then showed no new messages. The watch appears to read a workspace-level cursor, not the bound participant's, so a long-armed doorbell can fire a full-history replay that looks like a flood. A watch that names which cursor it reports, or reads the participant cursor when bound, would have prevented the false alarm.

Post c808283 added key/legacy to 'post profile show --json'; porch's exact-schema startup check (roomcheck.assert_acting_room) refused them and porch failed to launch on both hosts. The archive e2e called porch functions directly and skipped app startup, so it missed this. Prevention: post smoke should launch porch's startup checks (tests/test_post_live.py already does, against the installed post) before a post install is called done; and post->porch JSON additions need a contract note. Fixed in porch 39ca6df.

post watch --digest re-reported 344 old #jev-experiments messages as new after a transient 'cursor state ... not a solitary regular file' warning; participants/<id>/cursors.json was a normal 1-link regular file seconds later (concurrent .participant.json.*.tmp rename in flight). watch should retry the cursor read briefly before falling back to all-unread, or mark the replay unambiguously in the event line
post watch rejects --channel; channel selection belongs to the doorbell adapter rather than the watch CLI. A watch help example showing this distinction would prevent the failed probe.
Delegate completion notification passed --allow-self to the installed Post CLI, which rejected it; align the notify adapter with Post so unattended lane completion is delivered.

scripts/install-post.sh on the devbox needs CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$(estate-build-cache path)" or the build misses the shared cache. Would have prevented: the installer reading estate-build-cache itself when present.

post scripts/gate.sh has no timeout around cargo test, so one hanging test (lane R hit one tonight) stalls the whole gate with no output. Would have prevented: a per-suite timeout that names the stuck test binary.

post: the activation-notice write returns an I/O error when stderr is closed, so the command exits nonzero after doing its work (participant::emit_activation_notice). Deliberate to keep the notice pending, but callers see a failure. Would have prevented: a distinct exit or warning path for notice-only failures.

post watch --snapshot with an explicit but unknown POST_PARTICIPANT exits 0 with empty output and only 'participant: unbound' on stderr, which reads as 'no mail'. Would have prevented: a nonzero exit for an unknown explicit participant.

post: 8 concurrent 'post watch --snapshot' processes cost about 5x the CPU of one alone (lane E benchmark), likely lock spinning on the store. Would have prevented: a store lock that blocks instead of spins.

post read <id> consumes mail and silently drops a piped stdin body; the A2 stdin refusal covers channel reads only (reported by the lane R GLM review; not re-verified at 74dd1dd). Would have prevented: the same stdin guard on mail reads.

post channels fails outright when one channel message file is corrupt, instead of skipping it with a warning (lane D out-of-boundary finding). Would have prevented: per-message skip with skipped_unreadable.

post schema's watch event shape omits cursor_unusable and sender-provenance fields that watch emits (lane D finding), so consumers built from the schema miss them. Would have prevented: schema generated from the event type.

doorbell installers' snapshot probe only checks that each output line is a JSON object, so a wrong-shaped watch output passes the install probe (lane D finding). Would have prevented: probing the fields the doorbell reads.
legacy Python post-doorbell raises AttributeError in registered_rooms on a non-object listing (lane D finding). Superseded by the supervisor tonight but still installed where not migrated.

Porch's default owner marker is a fox and post's is a bearded face, so Porch's suggested 'post owner init' (which omits --marker) leaves the store signing-disabled. Would have prevented: one shared default, or Porch passing --marker.

delegate devin work: Devin's non-interactive run does not exit after finishing, so every run ends on the 8-min stall watchdog and the envelope reports error=stalled, ok=false, even when the work succeeded (2026-09-23: doorbell-cap run committed c6d98ba and wrote its report at ~17:19Z, then idled until cancelled). Costs 8 min per lane and makes success look like failure; a done-detector (report file written + no child process) or Devin's own exit signal would prevent it. A second SWE-2 max run on a large 9-finding brief went silent after 27 min with zero edits and was also cancelled as stalled.

post send prints 'post: sending as …' status lines on stderr even with --json, so 'post send --json 2>&1 | jq' fails to parse. That reads like a failed send, and a retry double-sent a note to cos-devbox (20260923-211941-dc6e90 and 212005-e7e22d). Prevention: stay silent on stderr under --json, or have --json always emit a result object on stdout that is safe to pipe.

post watch --from now in a Claude session on ~/Code/loom never printed a #loom-build message from a Loom-hosted Claude (participant loom-95286e23) while the UserPromptSubmit hook did report '#loom-build: 2 new'. Both identities resolve to room 'loom' (post chat reads 'reading as loom'), so same-room messages may be filtered from watch. A coordinator and its hosted agent sharing a repo share a room name; a doorbell that silently drops the other agent's messages looks healthy. Worked around with a Monitor polling post chat --history.

Post may drop a message to one of two watches on the same participant: lane B's Loom session (2026-09-24T0833-ab690d, ~08:45Z) probed direct mail between two throwaway participants, six runs; in one run the older watch missed a message within 3 s, and five reruns did not repeat it. Broadcast to every live watch is otherwise the observed model. Loom's handover design now depends on it. A Post-side look at watch delivery under two concurrent watches would settle whether it's a real race.

post: 'post chat night-porch --join' on the Mac silently created a new host-local channel while the established #night-porch (619 msgs, 16 members) lives on the devbox; neither v2 bridge allowlist (both 'loom-build' only) nor the cell bridge CHANNELS list carries it, so a Mac agent told 'post supports cross-machine channels now' splits the room without any hint. Would have prevented it: --join warning when a remote host advertises a same-name channel, or channels bridged by default per the porch's own description ('cross-cell, cross-machine'). Workaround used: devbox seat via ssh (post participant bind --new --workspace writing-plans) + ssh-wrapped post watch Monitor.
post who hung past a 10s timeout with no output while I was surveying participants read-only for a fleet review; a --timeout or a progress line on stderr would make a hang distinguishable from slow

post who --json hung 1m55s on the trey cell (09-25 12:52, 1m17s of it sys time) and returned exit 0. Loom's warp tail calls it synchronously at startup, so every loomw/loomp launch stalled 10 s until Loom bounded it at 2 s (loom 33b66b3). Worth profiling who: the sys time suggests a scan (store walk or lock spin), not network.

Codex hook error line '[post] POST_PARTICIPANT conflicts…' was injected as an instruction 5,284 times across 51 Codex sessions (found by context-waste recon lane). Prevention: fix the post hook so a config conflict logs once, not on every request.

post chat --json still prints a 'post: sending to #chan as room ...' banner on stderr; with 2>&1 the banner lands in front of the JSON and breaks jq, which reads like a failed send. Prevention: keep stderr separate (2>/dev/null or a file) when parsing --json, or drop the banner when --json is set.

post who --json took 76.7 s on the devbox (2026-09-26 22:20 CDT, rc 0); Loom's startup context step caps it at 2 s, so every Loom launch waits the full 2 s for it. Loom will stop blocking on it; Post itself should be profiled
